modules.name: Introduction of Plant Growth and Development

blocks.title: Core Concept
blocks.text:
Growth is regarded as one of the most fundamental and conspicuous characteristics of living beings.

• Irreversible, permanent increase in the size of an organ or its parts or cell.
    • Involves both catabolic and anabolic processes.
    • Plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life.
    • Plant growth generally is indeterminate.
    • Plants have an open form of growth.
PLANT GROWTH

Primary Growth

    • e.g. Growth due to root apical meristem and shoot apical meristem
    • Contribute to the elongation of plants along their axis.
Secondary Growth

    • e.g. In dicots and gymnosperms the lateral meristem is responsible for secondary growth
    • Vascular cambium
    • Cork cambium
GROWTH IS MEASURABLE

    • Growth is measured by a variety of parameters, some of which are :
    • Increase in fresh weight.
    • Increase in dry weight.
    • Increase in surface area/volume.
    • Increase in the number or size of cells.
    • Increase in length
    • Growth is measured by Auxanometer.
    • One single maize root apical meristem can give rise to more than 17,500 new cells per hour, whereas cells in watermelon may increase in size by up to 3,50,000 times.

blocks.title: Phases of Growth
blocks.text:
PHASES OF GROWTH

Meristematic Phase :

  • Constantly dividing cells at root and shoot apex
  • Cells are small in size
  • Abundant plasmodesmatal connections.
  • Cell wall is primary, thin and cellulosic.
  • Cells are rich in protoplasm
  • Large conspicuous nucleus.
Elongation Phase :

  • Cells proximal to meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation
Cells in this region show:

  • Increased vacuolation
  • Cell enlargement
  • New cell wall deposition.
Maturation Phase

  • Cells more proximal to phase of elongation represents the phase of maturation
Cells in this zone show maximal size in terms of:

  • Wall Thickening
  • Protoplasm modifications.

blocks.title: Question: 1
blocks.question:
The process of growth is maximum during:

(1) Dormancy

(2) Log phase

(3) Lag phase

(4) Senescence
blocks.answer:
Ans. (2)

Explanation:

  • The log phase (exponential phase) is the period of maximum growth during biological processes. Cells or organisms multiply rapidly, and growth occurs at its highest rate because the conditions (e.g., nutrients, energy) are optimal. This phase is common in microbial growth or organismal development.
blocks.prompt: The process of growth is maximum during:

blocks.title: Question: 2
blocks.question:
If the population of a bacteria culture doubles every hour, this is an example of:

1) Arithmetic growth
2) Geometric growth
3) Linear growth
4) Logarithmic growth
blocks.answer:
Answer: 2) Geometric growth

In geometric growth, the population increases exponentially, with each generation being a multiple of the previous one. In this case, the bacteria population doubles every hour, which is characteristic of geometric or exponential growth.

blocks.title: Question: 3
blocks.question:
In which of the following conditions do plants exhibit the best growth?

1) High carbon dioxide concentration and low light intensity
2) Optimal temperature, sufficient light, and adequate water availability
3) Excessive water and high temperature
4) Dark, high humidity, and low temperature
blocks.answer:
Answer: 2) Optimal temperature, sufficient light, and adequate water availability

Plants exhibit the best growth when they have access to the ideal combination of environmental conditions.

blocks.title: Differentiation, Dedifferentiation & Redifferentiation
blocks.text:
Differentiation :

  • Cell loses its ability to divide
  • Cells derived from root apical, shoot apical meristems and intra- fascicular cambium differentiate and mature to perform specific functions
  • Structural changes take place in cell wall and protoplasm
  • e.g. formation of tracheary elements
Dedifferentiation :

  • Differentiated cells regain the capacity to divide under certain conditions
  • e.g. Formation of secondary meristem (inter fascicular and cork cambium) from fully differentiated parenchyma cells.
Redifferentiation :

  • Dedifferentiated cells once again lose the capacity to divide and mature to perform specific function.
e.g. List of tissues in woody dicotyledonous plants that are the products of redifferentiation:

  • Secondary xylem
  • Secondary phloem
  • Cork or phellem
  • Secondary cortex
Differentiation in plants is open because cells/tissues arising out of the same meristem have different structures at maturity.

e.g. Cells positioned away from root apical meristems differentiate as root cap cells, while those pushed to the periphery mature as epidermis.

blocks.title: Plasticity
blocks.text:
The ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different structures is known as Plasticity,

Example: Heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur, in different phases of life. Different shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in Buttercup (Ranunculus)

blocks.title: Question:1
blocks.question:
The ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to the environment leading to the formation of different kinds of structures is called :

(1) Redifferentiation

(2) Development

(3) Plasticity

(4) Differentiation
blocks.answer:
Ans. (3)

Plasticity in plants refers to their ability to exhibit different growth patterns or form different structures in response to environmental conditions.
blocks.prompt: The ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to the environment leading to the formation of different kinds of structures is called :

blocks.title: Question:2
blocks.question:
Which of the following plants show different leaf forms at different stages of growth, an example of heterophylly?

1) Mango
2) Larkspur
3) Sunflower
4) Cucumber
blocks.answer:
Answer: 2) Larkspur

Heterophylly refers to the occurrence of different types of leaves on the same plant.

modules.name: Plant Growth Regulators' Characteristics and Discovery

blocks.title: Characteristics (Auxins & Gibberellins)
blocks.text:
AUXINS :

  • Apical Dominance
  • (Decapitation is done for hedge making and in tea plantation)
  • Cell division and enlargement
  • Root Initiation in stem cuttings
  • Prevent leaf and fruit drop at early stages but promote abscission of older mature leaves and fruits
  • Flower initiation in pineapple
  • Parthenocarpy in tomato
  • Weedicide for dicot (e.g., 2, 4-D)
Gibberellins :

  • Stem/Internode elongation
  • Used to speed up the malting process in brewing industry.
  • Increase the length of grapes stalks and cause fruits like apple to elongate & improve its shape.
  • Increase height of sugarcane stem and hence increase the yield
  • Delays senescence of fruits
  • Hastens maturity period of conifers
  • Bolting in beet and cabbage

blocks.title: Characteristics of Ethylene and Cytokinins
blocks.text:
Ethylene :

  • Ripening of fruits (Respiratory climactic)
  • Promotes senescence and abscission of fruits and flowers (Thinning of cotton, walnut & cherry)
  • Flowering and synchronizing fruiting in pineapple also induces flowering in mango.
  • Promotes root growth and root hair formation
  • Triple response on stem :
(a) Apical hook formation in dicot seedlings

(b) Swelling of axis

(c) Horizontal growth of seedlings

  • Induces femaleness in cucumber
  • Breaks seed dormancy in peanuts, and bud dormancy in potato
  • Internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice plants
Cytokinins :

  • Promotes Cell-Division
  • Overcomes apical dominance and promotes lateral growth and adventitious shoot formation
  • Delay leaf senescence by promoting nutrient mobilisation
  • Helps to produce new leaves and chloroplast

blocks.title: Characteristics (Absicic acid (ABA))
blocks.text:
ABSCISIC ACID (ABA)

  • Induces senescence & abscission
  • Plays an important role in seed development, maturation, and dormancy
  • ABA stimulates the closure of stomata and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses. It is also called the stress hormone.
  • Helps seed to withstand desiccation & other factors unfavorable for growth
  • ABA acts as a general plant growth inhibitor.
  • ABA acts as an antagonist to GAs (Gibberellins)

blocks.title: Example-1
blocks.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-l                                              List-II

(A) Auxin                                        (I) Promotes female flower formation in cucumber

(B) Gibberellin                                (II) Overcoming apical dominance

(C) Cytokinin                                  (III) Increase in the length of grape stalks

(D) Ethylene                                    (IV) Promotes flowering in pineapple

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

(1) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

(2) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

(3) (A)-(1), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

(4) (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
blocks.prompt:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-l                                              List-II

blocks.title: Example-2
blocks.question:
Which hormone promotes internode/ petiole elongation in deep-water rice?

(1) Kinetin

(2) Ethylene

(3) 2, 4-D

(4) $\mathrm{GA}_3$
blocks.answer:
Ans. (2)

Ethylene promotes the elongation of internodes and petioles in conditions like deep-water rice where the plant needs to grow taller to reach the water surface.
